definitions.explanation: A prefix used to refer to a person, place, or thing without specifying who or what it is. Used when the speaker deliberately conceals the identity or when the identity is unknown.

examples.japanese: {某|ぼう}{大学|だいがく}の{教授|きょうじゅ}が{発表|はっぴょう}した。
examples.english: A professor at a certain university made the announcement.

examples.japanese: {某|ぼう}{有名|ゆうめい}{企業|きぎょう}の{社長|しゃちょう}が{逮捕|たいほ}された。
examples.english: The president of a certain famous company was arrested.

examples.japanese: {関係者|かんけいしゃ}の{某氏|ぼうし}によると、{計画|けいかく}は{来月|らいげつ}{発表|はっぴょう}されるらしい。
examples.english: According to a certain person involved, the plan will apparently be announced next month.

notes:
Used to refer to a person, place, or organization without naming them. Common in news reporting, storytelling, and formal writing when the identity is either unknown or deliberately withheld.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {某|ぼう} + noun: {某|ぼう}{国|こく} (a certain country), {某|ぼう}{社|しゃ} (a certain company), {某|ぼう}{氏|し} (a certain person)
- {某|ぼう}{大学|だいがく} — a certain university
- {某|ぼう}{有名|ゆうめい}〜 — a certain famous ~

COMPOUNDS:
- {某氏|ぼうし} — a certain Mr./Ms.
- {某所|ぼうしょ} — a certain place
- {某国|ぼうこく} — a certain country
- {某日|ぼうじつ} — a certain day

REGISTER:
Fairly formal. In casual speech, people would say ある〜 (a certain ~) instead. {某|ぼう} is characteristic of news articles, official reports, and written narratives.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ある — a certain (more casual, everyday equivalent)
- {何某|なにがし} — somebody, so-and-so (more literary/archaic)
